doc.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024

title: Road band not playing on the records
summary: The touring band knew some tunes were beyond them and studio players handled those parts.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Were the musicians that were on the road in the working band, were they somewhat aggravated by not playing on the records?

Well some — you know they knew that certain tunes they wouldn’t be able to play. You know, like “Down and Out in New York City” I used that as an example because there was a lot of notes in there that they couldn’t reach, and a lot of rhythms that they couldn’t do. You know you had to have some skill to do what — some things I had to write out and they could look at it and then see it. But they understood that it was stuff they couldn’t do and I would have to get the real musicians to do it too. I say “real musicians” I mean the studious kind of learned musicians, to do it.
Yeah. And they could do it, probably the second time around if the parts had been prepared correctly.

Maybe the third time around. You know? Yeah. Things would happen like that you know. I’m sorry, I can’t remember this bass player’s name because we had so much — well we started out aggravated with each other you know, but we ended up being good friends.
